quick: 50-100 mg two to three times daily (max ~300 mg/day)
May be taken with or without food
Avoid - benzodiazepine class; insufficient safety data
Caution in renal impairment; limited data
Caution - hepatic metabolism (CYP3A4); avoid in significant impairment
Avoid - potential additive CNS effects despite low sedation
Anxiety/autonomic symptoms; mood; avoid dependence with prolonged use
summary: Tofisopam is an atypical 2,3-benzodiazepine used as a daytime anxiolytic for anxiety with prominent autonomic (somatic) symptoms. Unlike classic 1,4-benzodiazepines it has little sedative, anticonvulsant, muscle-relaxant, or memory-impairing effect, and lower dependence potential. NOTE: tofisopam is NOT FDA-approved in the United States; it is marketed in parts of Europe and Asia (e.g., Grandaxin) - prescribing follows the manufacturer SmPC.
indications: Anxiety, tension, and stress-related states, particularly with autonomic (somatic) symptoms
Mild alcohol withdrawal-related autonomic symptoms (where licensed)
admin: Take orally; the last dose should not be late in the evening for those sensitive to any stimulation
Use for the shortest period necessary; review need periodically
Avoid abrupt discontinuation after prolonged use
Avoid concomitant alcohol and other CNS depressants
moa: Tofisopam is a 2,3-benzodiazepine that modulates the GABA system differently from classic 1,4-benzodiazepines - it does not bind the conventional benzodiazepine site in a way that produces sedation, and is thought to act partly via dopaminergic and phosphodiesterase pathways. The result is anxiolytic and autonomic-stabilizing activity without significant sedative, hypnotic, anticonvulsant, or muscle-relaxant effects.

monitor: Mood and signs of dependence with prolonged use

preg: Avoid in pregnancy, especially the first trimester. As a benzodiazepine-class drug with insufficient human safety data, use is not recommended unless the benefit clearly outweighs the risk.
lact: Benzodiazepines are excreted in breast milk and can affect the infant. Avoid use during breastfeeding.
renal: Use with caution in renal impairment; limited pharmacokinetic data. Consider dose reduction.
hepatic: Metabolized in the liver (CYP3A4). Avoid or reduce dose in significant hepatic impairment; potent CYP3A4 inhibitors can raise levels.

moderate: CNS depressants and alcohol (additive CNS depression possible)
Potent CYP3A4 inhibitors (e.g., ketoconazole, ritonavir - increase tofisopam levels)
CYP3A4 inducers (e.g., rifampicin, carbamazepine - reduce levels)
interactions.food: May be taken with or without food

serious: Rare dependence with prolonged high-dose use
emergency: Respiratory depression in predisposed patients with CNS depressant co-use

monitoring: Signs of tolerance or dependence with prolonged use
Liver function if symptoms suggest hepatic effects
counsel: This medicine treats anxiety with body (autonomic) symptoms and is generally not sedating
Do not stop suddenly after long-term use - taper under medical guidance
Use only for as long as your doctor advises
Report rash, yellowing of skin/eyes, or marked mood changes
pk: Anxiolytic effect develops over the first days of treatment
Plasma peak ~2 hours after an oral dose
Store at controlled room temperature; protect from light and moisture
pearls: NOT FDA-approved in the US - marketed as Grandaxin in parts of Europe/Asia; prescribing follows the SmPC
An atypical 2,3-benzodiazepine: anxiolytic without significant sedation, muscle relaxation, anticonvulsant effect, or memory impairment, with lower dependence potential
Useful when autonomic/somatic symptoms predominate; does not impair psychomotor performance as much as classic benzodiazepines
A CYP3A4 substrate - watch for interactions with strong inhibitors/inducers
missed: Take the missed dose when remembered unless it is close to the next scheduled dose, in which case skip it. Do not double doses.
overdose: Overdose has a relatively wide margin of safety compared with classic benzodiazepines; it may cause vomiting, confusion, and (with large amounts or co-ingestants) CNS depression. Management is supportive with airway protection and monitoring; flumazenil is generally not effective because tofisopam does not act at the classic benzodiazepine site.
